stem: A model of Plasmodium falciparum sequestration uses erythrocytes containing mature trophozoites. Investigators pass equal numbers through two endothelial-lined chambers. A selective intervention prevents adherence in chamber X but leaves chamber Y untreated. The cells are otherwise unchanged. Which of the following paired results best supports adhesion as the retention mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Equal cells retained in X; equal cells exiting X
options.explanation: Equal distributions would fail to demonstrate an effect of blocking adherence. The proposed mechanism predicts that retention changes when the attachment step is selectively prevented.
options.misconception: Assumes blocking the proposed attachment mechanism leaves retention and exit unchanged.

options.label: B
options.text: Fewer cells retained in X; more cells exiting X
options.explanation: Preventing endothelial adherence reduces sequestration on the chamber surface. With the same input and otherwise unchanged cells, more infected erythrocytes should leave rather than remain attached.
options.misconception: No misconception: With fixed input, blocking adherence shifts cells from retention toward exit.

options.label: C
options.text: More cells retained in X; fewer cells exiting X
options.explanation: This reverses the effect of preventing adherence. Increased retention would indicate greater sequestration, whereas the intervention removes the binding process that holds cells on the surface.
options.misconception: Reverses the effect of blocking adherence by predicting greater retention.

options.label: D
options.text: Fewer cells retained in X; fewer cells exiting X
options.explanation: Reduced retention fits the intervention, but reduced exit would require an additional unmeasured destination or cell loss. The experiment isolates attachment while preserving the cellular input.
options.misconception: Allows both retention and exit to fall without identifying another destination for the fixed cell input.

options.label: E
options.text: More cells retained in X; more cells exiting X
options.explanation: With matched input and no other cellular change, increasing both retained and exiting cells violates the comparison’s accounting. Prevented adherence should shift cells from retention toward exit.
options.misconception: Increases both retained and exiting cells despite equal input and no other cellular change.

context: Learning objective: Connect endothelial adherence of mature falciparum-infected erythrocytes to sequestration. A selective block should redistribute a fixed cell input from the retained compartment toward the exiting compartment.
